status_reasoning: Reviewers explicitly stated the data is 'convincing and comprehensive' and 'of high quality' regarding the mutagenesis screen that identified F876L. They affirmed the finding that this mutation converts enzalutamide into an AR agonist, with no challenges to the reporter-based screen methodology or the transcriptional activity data showing agonist conversion.

Reviewers accepted the cell proliferation and xenograft data showing that AR F876L rescues growth inhibition by enzalutamide. They suggested an additional in vivo experiment with novel antagonists (point 1) but explicitly stated this was 'not necessary for publication given the overall depth of the studies,' indicating acceptance of the existing in vivo resistance data.

Reviewers did not challenge the data showing spontaneous emergence of F876L in cell lines and xenografts under prolonged drug treatment. In point 7, they asked about other mutations identified in resistant tumors, indicating interest in additional context rather than skepticism about the F876L findings themselves.

Reviewers acknowledged 'nice rendering of AR-ligand structures' but stated 'it is not clear exactly in what way the F876L change results in altered interaction' (point 2). They requested additional figures showing distances and specific contacts (points 4-5), indicating the structural mechanism is plausible but needs clearer presentation to be fully convincing.

Reviewers accepted the rational drug design findings showing that DR103 and related compounds antagonize AR F876L. They requested clarification on potency comparisons and binding affinity data (point 6) and suggested testing enantiomers (point 9), but these are refinements rather than challenges to the core finding that the compounds work as designed.

Reviewers requested detailed distance measurements and discussion of how DR103 interacts with residue 876 in both WT and mutant receptors (points 4-5). While they did not reject the proposed mechanism of H12 displacement, they indicated the structural basis needs more explicit demonstration and discussion to be fully convincing.

Reviewers noted that 'bicalutamide appears to be an antagonist on F876L AR in some Figures but an agonist in others' and requested this be 'commented upon' (point 8). This indicates confusion about the pharmacology of bicalutamide against AR F876L, suggesting the data presentation needs clarification rather than indicating clear support or rejection.

Reviewers stated 'the paper would be strengthened by evidence that the F876L mutation does indeed occur in PCa patients' and suggested discussing this as a future direction (point 3). This indicates the clinical relevance is plausible but not yet demonstrated, with reviewers acknowledging 'it may be too soon for ENZ-resistant patients to have emerged.'
